blocks.text: Every focus area traces back to the evidence behind it and forward to its initiative and indicators, with a rating for the strength of that evidence.

The first table sets out what the evidence supports for each focus area and rates its strength on a three-point scale: strong, adequate or thin. The second table traces each focus area back to its workstream and the sections that discuss it, and forward to its initiative and indicators.

blocks.caption: Strength of evidence by focus area
blocks.source: Reading and strength from the evidence notes behind Chapter 3. Strong: the figure and finding are printed in two deliverables or in one with a full table. Adequate: supported, with a figure missing, different or from one source. Thin: side mentions only.
rows: 1 Respond to growth segment traveller preferences
Four segments confirmed against markets of high incidence; the segmentation is directional and leaves out the domestic and seven African markets
2 Create green-season demand with MICE and events
June holds 6.4% of 2025 international seat capacity; ICCA meetings 33 to 58 from 2022 to 2024
3 Make the whole province findable and bookable
CapeNature takes about 70% of reservations through its call centre, and community product sells by phone; no count of bookable products exists
4 Convert India and China hub traffic
About 101,000 journeys a year via hubs, the sum of two printed estimates, 71,000 and 30,000; the hub tables sum to 97,579
Five mature long-haul routes above 80% load; no fare or yield data
Nigeria R31,000 and Ghana R27,700 a visit, read as spend per visitor; the printed averages do not reproduce from the totals
7 Win direct routes and add seats on full routes

Eleven of 27 routes run above 80% load and sixteen at 75% or more, and carriers are expected to raise fares before adding seats; no frequency, aircraft-size or peak-slot data shows where seats can be added
79 vessels (Diagnostic) against 83 calls (Infrastructure Report) in 2024/25; a plan to 250 calls appears in no deliverable
Accessibility falls from 4.7 to 1.0 on the attractions and services basis; the transport basis gives 5.0 to 1.0
10 Support diversified route and product development
Cold zones, the Infrastructure Report's term for areas with tourism assets but little or no tourism use; no count of idle assets
A mid-scale gap, stated in words; no room or bed count
Stakeholder statements and queue times; no visitor counts or caps for any flagship
13 Embed local destination bodies for community inclusion
Seller with a stake, 20 communities and R259m a year at 1% of FY2025 foreign direct spend; one page prints 18 shortlisted, and the spend-tracing method is not described
14 Manage climate risk and sustainable tourism
LTO funding disrupted and Meiringspoort closed, from two organisations' statements and the Inclusion Plan's De Rust profile
15 Crowd in capital with targeted investment strategies
An inference: a large capital pipeline exists and almost none of it reaches regional product, SME bookability or township product
16 Align institutional stakeholders across all three tiers
Air rights and visas sit nationally, as the Diagnostic's tier table shows; no decision-rights map exists
Raised by 15 of 16 organisations, a reconstructed count of organisations, not insight rows
18 Expedite tourism-enabling policy and data sharing
Platforms exist; no data-sharing protocol in progress is described
19 Lead removal of infrastructure, visa and safety deficits
Levers sit nationally for visas and air rights; safety programmes are provincial and basic services local
No provincial tourism employment baseline in any deliverable; the labour analysis is still to be commissioned
blocks.message: Nine focus areas rest on strong evidence and ten on adequate evidence; only focus area 20 is thin, and several figures hold only with a qualifier.

rows: 1 Respond to growth segment traveller preferences

MIDAS seasonality (June 6.4% of international seats) and the Demand-Side MICE section (ICCA, UIA)

Demand-Side route-to-market (71,000 India and 30,000 China via hubs) and MIDAS (same figures; no direct route before 2030)
MIDAS (mature long-haul routes above 80% load; carriers raise fares before adding seats) with the Demand-Side mature-market projection
Demand-Side African opportunity section and Skift African memo; MIDAS regional route loads

MIDAS Aviation Market Assessment; Infrastructure Report air-access section
Diagnostic cruise table and Infrastructure Report cruise and ports section; Wesgro cruise reports (not in hand)
Infrastructure Report comparative regional analysis; Stakeholder Insights (Department of Mobility)
10 Support diversified route and product development
Infrastructure Report spatial maps and route scorecards; Stakeholder Insights (11 of 16 organisations)
Infrastructure Report accommodation mapping; Stakeholder Insights (service quality); Benchmarking (Valencia, Singapore)
Stakeholder Insights (Boulders near capacity, Table Mountain queues); Infrastructure Report flagship congestion
13 Embed local destination bodies for community inclusion

Stakeholder Insights (MFMA Circular No. 131, LTO sustainability, climate losses); Inclusion plan De Rust profile (Meiringspoort closed 6 May 2026)

Infrastructure Report pipeline and gap-closure tables (gaps with no committed capital); Stakeholder Insights (funding below peers); Benchmarking (Chile concession, New Zealand route fund)

Stakeholder Insights (bilateral air agreements, fragmented mandates); Diagnostic governance tiers; MIDAS (government-to-government route designation)
Stakeholder Insights appendix tables, counted for this report (Appendix A6)

Stakeholder Insights (JAMS, statistics committees, Stats SA task team); Skift digital memo (tracking framework)
19 Lead removal of infrastructure, visa and safety deficits
Stakeholder Insights, Demand-Side barriers and MIDAS all place visas and air rights with national government
No workstream; prompted by the 300,000-jobs ambition (Inception p4) and skills mentions in the Stakeholder Insights and Inclusion plan
